cases.query: What is a common first-line medication approach for type 2 diabetes?
cases.expected_answer: Clinical guidelines commonly describe metformin as a standard first-line therapy for type 2 diabetes, depending on patient-specific factors.
cases.actual_answer:
Metformin is the common first-line medication for type 2 diabetes, typically started alongside lifestyle modification and glycemic monitoring when there are no contraindications. Bootstrap guideline summaries note that treatment is often individualized afterward, with escalation to GLP-1 receptor agonists, SGLT2 inhibitors, or insulin depending on comorbidities, kidney function, cardiovascular risk, and glycemic control. A PubMed-indexed guideline review (Diabetes, Obesity & Metabolism, 2024; PMID 38992869) similarly describes metformin as foundation therapy recommended by most national, regional, and international guidelines, while also noting debate about its first-line role in some guidelines.

This is general guideline information rather than individualized medical advice; specific treatment decisions should be made with a qualified clinician.

cases.query: What kinds of information do hypertension guidelines usually provide?
cases.expected_answer: Hypertension guidelines generally cover diagnosis thresholds, blood pressure targets, medication classes, and follow-up recommendations.
cases.actual_answer: Hypertension guidelines generally cover blood pressure thresholds and target ranges, along with guidance on home blood pressure monitoring and lifestyle changes. They also describe medication classes used in treatment, such as ACE inhibitors, ARBs, calcium-channel blockers, and thiazide-type diuretics. Follow-up timing is typically tailored to the severity of hypertension, the presence of symptoms, and how a patient responds to treatment.

cases.query: Why should retrieved medical guidance include a disclaimer?
cases.expected_answer: Medical RAG systems should clarify that outputs are educational and not a substitute for clinician judgment or personalized care.
cases.actual_answer: Retrieved medical guidance should include a disclaimer stating that the information is for educational purposes only and is not a substitute for clinician judgment, diagnosis, or personalized treatment. This matters because it clarifies the limits of the material being presented and encourages users to consult qualified healthcare professionals. (Source: Bootstrap, guideline summary on disclaimers for medical guidance.)
